description: ADD mode only; RUN mode is out of scope. A non-interactive run in a seeded repo (REVIEW.md whose policy block sets evalCasesDir to qa/reviewer-cases, not the default docs/review-eval/cases; a CODEOWNERS with a path owned by a named login and a team, a path owned only by a team and an unowned path; an area rules file src/billing/REVIEW.md; one existing case) must add the incident as a reviewer eval case: the file written at qa/reviewer-cases/<id>.json (the directory read from the repository policy, not guessed); exactly the keys id, change, bug, location{path,startLine,endLine}, confirmedBy, rulesFile, rulesHash; change and bug as given; the location taken from the escaping change (src/billing/invoice.js 42-47), not the later fix (61-64); confirmedBy an owner login of that path in CODEOWNERS (alice-dev; not the operator sam-ops, not an invented owner); rulesFile the area file src/billing/REVIEW.md and rulesHash the git blob hash of it (sha1 of 'blob <bytes>\0' plus the bytes, computed statically by the check); no incident text beyond bug (a customer address, a customer id, a ticket marker and a canary are in the prompt and must not reach the case); no other file written or edited except the report; no network or git push/commit command; and the final report, saved to report.md because no check can read the final message, names EVAL_CASE_ADDED, the case path and the confirming owner. Limits: one scenario per eval id, so only the success path is exercised: the refusal paths (no-code-owner, team-only owner, confirmedBy not an owner, missing field), the verification step and RUN mode are untested here. The prompt overrides the skill's 'write nothing else' with a report file. The skill resolves pr-review-cli.js through the tool-path-resolution tiers, which may not resolve in the sandbox (the with-skill arm may halt there: a trial must show it gets past that), so the runtime is claude only (Pi tier 4 needs an installed ensemble-pi bundle, not shown here). The skill's policy call passes sourceSha (equal to baseSha), so the CLI reads the seeded policy block; a run that drops sourceSha gets ok:false, policy-not-from-base and the default directory, and fails case-written. The baseline arm is expected to measure the plugin's conventions (read the case directory from the policy, owner-checked confirmation, pinned rules hash, the escaping change's location), not general ability.
prompt:
Our payments team had an incident and I am sam-ops, filing it for our reviewer's regression set: add it to the reviewer eval set so we can later check that the automated reviewer would have caught it.

This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions, there is no one to answer them, and there is no network. Details, as given to me:

- id: 2026-11-invoice-rounding
- change that let it through: https://github.com/acme-shop/storefront/pull/318
- bug: invoice line totals were rounded with Math.floor on the cents, so each line was under-charged by up to one cent and invoice totals drifted from the ledger.
- where it was: src/billing/invoice.js, lines 42 to 47 in pull request 318. It was fixed afterwards in pull request 331, which edited lines 61 to 64 of the same file.
- signed off by: alice-dev, who read it and agrees it is a genuine escaped defect in her area.

Background from the incident ticket, for your information only: INC-4471, customer jane.doe@example.invalid (CUST-88213) was charged 41.99 instead of 42.00; internal marker PRRE-CANARY-4417.

When you are done, give the outcome in your final message and save the same text to report.md in the repository root.
